questions.question: Identify the correct type of sentence used in the line: "As the world races to meet net-zero targets, emissions from all industrial sectors must be reduced more urgently than ever".
questions.solution:
A complex sentence contains one independent clause and at least one dependent (or subordinate) clause.

Independent Clause: "emissions from all industrial sectors must be reduced more urgently than ever"

This is a complete thought and can stand alone as a sentence.

Dependent Clause: "As the world races to meet net-zero targets"

This clause begins with the subordinating conjunction "As." It has a subject ("world") and a verb ("races"), but it cannot stand alone as a complete sentence. It depends on the independent clause to make sense.

Since the sentence has one independent clause and one dependent clause, it is a complex sentence.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

Option (b): A simple sentence contains only one independent clause and no dependent clauses. An independent clause has a subject and a verb and expresses a complete thought.

Option (c): A compound-complex sentence is a combination of a compound sentence and a complex sentence. It must contain at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.

Option (d): A compound sentence consists of at least two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (like for, and, but, or, so) or a semicolon. Both clauses can stand alone as complete sentences.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

My grandfather told me that while he worked at the old mill, the entire town depended on its productivity for their livelihood.
options: My grandfather said to me, "While I was working at the old mill, the entire town depended on its productivity for their livelihood."
My grandfather said to me, "While he had worked at the old mill, the entire town had depended on its productivity for their livelihood."

questions.solution:
If the sentence in Indirect Speech is in Simple Past and is used in a time clause (starting with 'when', 'while', etc.), the form of the tense doesn't change when converted to Direct Speech.

The reporting verb 'told' is changed to 'said to'. The pronoun 'he' is changed to 'I'.

For example:

Ayush told me that when he saw him, he was working. (Indirect Speech)

Ayush said to me, "When I saw him, he was working". (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'Told' is changed into 'said to'.

'That' is removed.

'He worked' is changed into 'I worked'.

The tense of the sentence does not change.

Also, inverted commas ("...") are placed in direct speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is: My grandfather said to me, "While I worked at the old mill, the entire town depended on its productivity for their livelihood."

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:

options: The manager said to the new intern, "He is reviewing the quarterly performance report for the upcoming board meeting."

The manager said to the new intern, "I was reviewing the quarterly performance report for the upcoming board meeting."
The manager said to the new intern, "You are reviewing the quarterly performance report for the upcoming board meeting."
questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'Told' is changed into 'said to'.

'That' is removed.

'He' is changed into 'I'.

'Was reviewing' is changed into 'am reviewing'.

Also, inverted commas ("...") are placed in direct speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The manager said to the new intern, "I am reviewing the quarterly performance report for the upcoming board meeting."

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Can the logistics department arrange the immediate dispatch of these urgent medical supplies to the disaster-stricken area?
options: Could the immediate dispatch of these urgent medical supplies be arranged by the logistics department for the disaster-stricken area?
Can the immediate dispatch of these urgent medical supplies be arranged by the logistics department to the disaster-stricken area?
The immediate dispatch of these urgent medical supplies to the disaster-stricken area can be arranged by the logistics department.
Will the logistics department be arranging the immediate dispatch of these urgent medical supplies to the disaster-stricken area?
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The question in the Active voice is an interrogative sentence. This type of sentence begins with a Modal Auxiliary verb.

The format of such a sentence in the Active voice is: Modal + Subject + V1 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Modal + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)?

The modal verb 'Can' should remain unchanged.

For example:

Can you do this? (Active)

Can this be done by you? (Passive)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is option (b).

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.question:
Select the sentence which gives the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A storm in a teacup
options: The category five hurricane caused widespread destruction and chaos throughout the entire coastal region.
The two leaders had a very serious and consequential discussion about international trade policies.
There was a huge argument over a minor issue that was quickly forgotten the next day.
She remained calm and composed during the crisis, providing clear instructions to her whole team.
questions.solution:
The idiom "a storm in a teacup" (or "a tempest in a teapot") refers to a great deal of anger, excitement, or worry about a trivial or unimportant matter.

Option (a): This describes a literal, major storm with serious consequences, not a trivial issue. Incorrect.

Option (b): This describes a serious and important discussion, the opposite of the idiom's meaning. Incorrect.

Option (c): This sentence describes a big argument over a minor, unimportant issue, which is the precise meaning of the idiom. Correct.

Option (d): This describes remaining calm, which is contrary to the fuss and anger implied by the idiom. Incorrect.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the proverb from the options.

You cannot make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.
options: Training always converts weak inputs into premium results
Superior outcomes require suitable materials; you can't transform the inherently poor into the truly fine
Presentation can hide all defects permanently
questions.solution:
The proverb means that it is impossible to create something of high quality (a silk purse) from something that is inherently of low quality or unsuitable (a sow's ear). The quality of the starting materials or the fundamental nature of a person or thing limits what can be made from it.

This explanation aligns with option (b).

Usage: The designer tried to improve the poorly built house, but you cannot make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The spies arranged a clandestine meeting to exchange the secret documents. What is the ANTONYM of 'clandestine'?
questions.solution:
"Clandestine" means kept secret or done secretively, especially because it is illicit or forbidden.

The opposite is "overt", which means done or shown openly; not secret or hidden.

Option (b) Dangerous: describes a potential quality of a clandestine meeting, but it is not its opposite.

Option (c) Secretive: is a synonym for 'clandestine'.

Option (d) Urgent: describes the timing or necessity of the meeting, not its level of secrecy.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1: Getting enough quality sleep is not a luxury; it is a biological necessity. P: During deep sleep, the body also works to repair muscles, tissues, and strengthen the immune system. Q: A chronic lack of it can lead to impaired cognitive function, mood swings, and long-term health problems. R: This is because the brain is highly active while we sleep, consolidating memories and processing information from the day. S: Beyond these mental benefits, sleep is crucial for physical restoration. 6: Therefore, prioritizing sleep is one of the most fundamental things we can do for our overall well-being.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is b) RSPQ.

The paragraph explains why sleep is necessary by listing its benefits and the consequences of its absence.

Opening Statement (1): Makes a strong claim about the necessity of sleep.

Sentence R: This explains the primary reason for the claim in sentence 1 ("This is because..."). It starts by explaining the mental or cognitive role of sleep.

Sentence S: The phrase "Beyond these mental benefits" creates a perfect transition from the cognitive aspects mentioned in R to the physical aspects of sleep. This establishes a clear R-S link.

Sentence P: This sentence provides specific examples of the "physical restoration" introduced in S, such as repairing muscles.

Sentence Q: After listing the benefits (R, S, P), this sentence presents the negative consequences of a "lack of it," which provides a contrast and reinforces the importance of sleep before the conclusion.

Closing Statement (6): The word "Therefore" indicates a conclusion that logically follows from the evidence presented (both positive and negative).

Therefore, the sequence that flows from mental benefits to physical benefits to the consequences of deprivation is RSPQ.

questions.question:
Rearrange the steps for mailing a package in the correct order:

P. Take the sealed and addressed package to the post office to pay for postage.

Q. Place the item securely inside an appropriate-sized box with padding.

R. Write the recipient's address clearly on the outside of the box.

S. Seal the box firmly with strong packing tape.
questions.solution:
The correct order is a) Q → S → R → P.

(Q): The first step is to put the contents inside the container.

(S): The box must be sealed to protect its contents. This happens before addressing.

(R): The package needs an address to be sent anywhere. This is done on the sealed box.

(P): This is the final step, which can only be completed after the package is packed, sealed, and addressed.

questions.question:
Which of the given options is the most logical sequencing of the following sentences to form a meaningful paragraph?

A. When environmental factors interact with the DNA, they can cause changes in the way certain characteristics show up.

B. For example, early exposure to toxic substances and stress can increase the risk of diseases later in childhood or in adulthood - particularly diseases that are not spread from one person to another, like dental caries, obesity, and diabetes.

C. During the first 1,000 days, children experience rapid growth, and they are more sensitive to interactions with the environment they live in.

D. Environmental factors, such as diet, substances in the air like cigarette smoke, and stress, can change the activity of genes - stretches of DNA that are responsible for creating most of a person's characteristics.
questions.solution:
Sentence C introduces the time frame of the first 1,000 days and highlights the sensitivity of children during this period to environmental interactions. It sets the context for the discussion about how environmental factors impact development.

Sentence D builds on sentence C by explaining how the environment affects children during this critical period. It specifically introduces environmental factors and links them to changes in gene activity, providing a scientific explanation for the sensitivity mentioned in sentence C. The connection between children's growth and gene-environment interaction logically follows.

After sentence D introduces the impact of environmental factors on gene activity, sentence A further expands this idea by stating that these interactions can affect how characteristics are expressed. Sentence A is a general statement that elaborates on the mechanism of how environmental factors affect physical or biological traits, which fits after the explanation of gene activity in sentence D.

Sentence B serves as a specific example of the general concept introduced in sentence A. After the more theoretical explanation in 'A', this sentence provides concrete examples of how environmental interactions with DNA can result in specific health outcomes, such as obesity or diabetes, reinforcing the ideas laid out in the previous sentences.

So, the correct order is CDAB.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The rare diamond necklace was stolen from the museum's high-security vault late last night.
options: They stole the rare diamond necklace from the museum's high-security vault late last night.
Somebody stole the rare diamond necklace from the museum's high-security vault late last night.

Stealing the rare diamond necklace from the museum's high-security vault happened late last night.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['was' in the given sentence] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In the Passive voice sentence, the agent (the one performing the action) is not mentioned. This is a case of a vague pronoun. In the Active voice, the introduction of "Somebody" or "Someone" is necessary for these types of sentences.

The sentence in the Passive voice is in Past Indefinite ['was stolen']. So, the sentence in the Active voice should also be in Past Indefinite ['stole'].

For example:

I have been robbed. (Passive)

Somebody has robbed me. (Active)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.solution:

In the context of the passage, "succumb" refers to tourists who fall victim to high-altitude sickness, meaning they suffer or die from the effects of it. questions.question: What is the primary cause of high-altitude sickness, as mentioned in the passage?
options: The body's inability to adjust to reduced oxygen levels.
Overexertion during physical activities at high elevations.
Inadequate hydration due to lack of water sources.
questions.solution:
Refer to the following excerpt from the first paragraph - "High-altitude sickness, or Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS), occurs when the body cannot acclimatise to high elevations, typically over 8,000 feet (2,400 metres). As altitude increases, the air pressure and oxygen levels decrease, leading to hypoxia - a shortage of oxygen in the body's tissues." So, this condition occurs when because of the increase in altitude, the air pressure and oxygen levels decrease, causing hypoxia (which is the primary cause of AMS).

Acclimatise: become accustomed to a new climate or new conditions; adjust.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Option (a): While extreme temperatures might pose challenges, the passage focuses on reduced air pressure and oxygen levels as the primary cause of high-altitude sickness.

Option (c): The passage doesn't mention overexertion as a cause of AMS, though it may worsen the condition.

Option (d): Hydration isn't discussed as a cause of AMS in the passage.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the correct use of the verb form.
options: These regions presents hidden dangers due to their extreme altitudes.
If left untreated, it can escalated into high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE), a life-threatening condition where fluid accumulates in the lungs
Yet, most high-altitude regions lacks this kind of infrastructure.
Leh, in the Union Territory of Ladakh, serves as a model, having developed specialised facilities for high-altitude ailments.
questions.solution:
Option (a): Error: Subject-verb agreement. The subject "regions" is plural, so the verb should be plural "present", not the singular "presents".

Correct: "These regions present hidden dangers..."

Option (b): Error: Incorrect verb form after a modal verb. Modal verbs (like "can," "will," "should") must be followed by the base form of the verb.

Correct: "...it can escalate into..."

Option (c): Error: Subject-verb agreement. The subject "most high-altitude regions" is plural, so the verb should be plural "lack", not the singular "lacks".

Correct: "...most high-altitude regions lack this kind of infrastructure."

Option (d): The singular verb "serves" is correctly used for the singular subject "Leh".

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The construction company is currently building a state-of-the-art sports complex right in the city centre.
options: A state-of-the-art sports complex was being built right in the city centre by the construction company.
A state-of-the-art sports complex is currently being built right in the city centre by the construction company.
A state-of-the-art sports complex is currently built right in the city centre by the construction company.
In the city centre, the construction company is building a state-of-the-art sports complex currently.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ['being' in the given sentence] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of the Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

The author and the publisher was thrilled with the overwhelming positive reception of their latest book, which quickly became a bestseller.
options: positive reception of their latest book,
questions.solution:
The subject "The author and the publisher" is made up of two different individuals: "the author" and "the publisher." When two singular nouns are joined by "and", each having a preceding 'the', they form a compound subject, which is considered plural. Therefore, the verb should be in the plural form "were" instead of the singular form "was." Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Note: A compound subject is a subject in a sentence that consists of two or more nouns, pronouns, or noun phrases joined by a coordinating conjunction (such as "and" or "or") that share the same verb.

The correct sentence: The author and the publisher were thrilled with the overwhelming positive reception of their latest book, which quickly became a bestseller.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The committee of experienced teachers, along with the principal, were responsible for organizing the annual school fair successfully.
questions.solution:
The error is in the segment "were responsible". The subject of the sentence is "The committee". "Committee" is a collective noun which, in this context, is treated as a single unit, hence it takes a singular verb. The phrase "along with the principal" is a prepositional phrase and does not affect the number of the subject for verb agreement. Therefore, the singular verb "was" should be used instead of the plural verb "were".

The correct sentence is: The committee of experienced teachers, along with the principal, was responsible for organizing the annual school fair successfully.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Collective Noun: It is the name given to a number (or collection) of persons or things taken together and spoken of as one whole. Examples could be crowd, fleet, committee, family, army, jury, heard, etc.

· Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement.

· Prepositional phrase: A modifying phrase consisting of a preposition and its object.

questions.question: The figure of speech used in "There was deafening silence in the room"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option b) Oxymoron.

An oxymoron is a figure of speech that combines two contradictory or opposite terms in a single phrase. The phrase "deafening silence" is a classic example. "Deafening" implies an extremely loud noise. "Silence" is the complete absence of noise. Putting these two opposite ideas together creates a powerful effect, emphasising that the silence was so profound and intense that it was overwhelming.

Hyperbole is an exaggeration, and while "deafening silence" has an exaggerative quality, its core structure is the combination of opposites, making oxymoron the more specific and accurate term.

A metaphor makes a direct comparison.

Alliteration is the repetition of initial sounds.

questions.question: Which among the following sentences uses the adjective with the correct degree of comparison?
options: In my opinion, that was the most worst movie of the year.
In my opinion, that was the worse movie of the year.
In my opinion, that was the baddest movie of the year.
In my opinion, that was the worst movie of the year.
questions.solution:
The adjective "bad" is irregular. Its comparative form is "worse", and its superlative form is "worst."

· Option (a): Incorrect. This is a double superlative. "Worst" is already the superlative form of "bad," so adding "most" is redundant and grammatically incorrect.

· Option (b): Incorrect. "Worse" is the comparative degree, used to compare two things (e.g., "This movie is worse than the last one"). Since the sentence is comparing one movie to all others "of the year," the superlative degree is required.

· Option (c): Incorrect. "Baddest" is a non-standard, informal superlative. The correct superlative form is "worst."

· Option (d): Correct. The sentence correctly uses the superlative form "worst" to compare the movie to a group of three or more (all movies of the year). It also correctly uses the definite article "the."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article, 'the'; it refers to or introduces a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question: What type of pronoun is the word "who" in the sentence, "Rohan and Saurabh were two ambitious entrepreneurs who embarked on a journey to create their own startup"?
questions.solution:
A relative pronoun introduces a clause that gives more information about a noun. It connects a dependent clause to a main clause.

In the given sentence, "who" connects the descriptive clause "embarked on a journey to create their own startup" back to the noun "entrepreneurs," making it a relative pronoun.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Option (a): An indefinite pronoun refers to a person, place, or thing that is not specific. It doesn't point to a particular noun.

Option (b): A reflexive pronoun is used when the subject of the sentence is also the object. It "reflects" back to the subject and ends in "-self" or "-selves."

Option (c): A possessive pronoun shows ownership or possession and replaces a noun. It answers the question, "Whose?"

questions.solution:

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

My colleague said to me, "Let us prepare a detailed presentation for the client meeting to impress the new board members."
options: My colleague said to me that they should prepare a detailed presentation for the client meeting to impress the new board members.
My colleague proposed me to prepare a detailed presentation for the client meeting to impress the new board members.
My colleague suggested that let us prepare a detailed presentation for the client meeting to impress the new board members.
My colleague proposed to me that we should prepare a detailed presentation for the client meeting to impress the new board members.
questions.solution:
When "Let" is used as a proposal/suggestion, "said/said to" is changed to "proposed/proposed to" or "suggested/suggested to". "That" is added, "Let" is removed, and the modal verb "should" is added before the main verb.

For example:

He said, "Let us go to the amusement park." (Direct Speech)

He suggested that they should go to the amusement park. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"said to" changes to "proposed to".

The conjunction "that" is added.

"Let us prepare" changes to "we should prepare".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "My colleague proposed to me that we should prepare a detailed presentation for the client meeting to impress the new board members."

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Doping a semiconductor with Boron would result in a p-type semiconductor.

Semiconductors like Silicon and Germanium belong to Group 14 and have four valence electrons. To create a p-type ("positive-type") semiconductor, they must be doped with a trivalent impurityan element with three valence electrons.

Boron is a Group 13 element and has three valence electrons. When a Boron atom replaces a Silicon atom in the crystal lattice, it can only form three covalent bonds with its neighbors. This leaves a vacancy or a "hole" where the fourth electron should be. This hole acts as a positive charge carrier, making the material a p-type semiconductor.

Explanation of Other Options:

(a) Lead: Lead is in Group 14, the same group as Silicon and Germanium. It has four valence electrons and would not act as a dopant to create p-type or n-type semiconductors.

(b) Arsenic: Arsenic is a Group 15 element with five valence electrons (a pentavalent impurity). When used as a dopant, it provides an extra electron, resulting in an n-type (negative-type) semiconductor.

(c) Phosphorous: Phosphorous is also a Group 15 element with five valence electrons. Like Arsenic, it is a pentavalent impurity and would create an n-type semiconductor.

Further insights:

Trivalent impurities like Boron, Aluminium, Gallium, and Indium are called acceptor impurities because they create holes that can "accept" electrons.

Pentavalent impurities like Phosphorous, Arsenic, and Antimony are called donor impurities because they "donate" an extra electron to the crystal lattice.
